industry: Electronic Design Automation (EDA) Software and Semiconductor IP
thesis: Synopsys is one half of the EDA duopoly that gates every advanced chip design, and the July 2025 Ansys acquisition extends that toll booth from silicon into system-level simulation. Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 42% to $2.477B with non-GAAP EPS of $3.91 beating guidance, Design IP returned to year-over-year growth, and management raised FY2026 guidance to ~$9.715B revenue and ~$15.07 non-GAAP EPS. The stock is down ~13% over the past year on AI-disruption fear, Intel and China exposure, and Ansys integration noise, leaving it at ~28x FY2026 non-GAAP EPS versus a ~$575 consensus target. The main risk is that the same AI that drives design complexity eventually automates away seat-based EDA revenue faster than Synopsys can monetize it.

financials.cash: $3.61B cash and short-term investments (2026-07-31) vs $10.04B total debt

drivers: EDA grows double digits as AI, multi-die and physical-AI designs raise tool intensity per chip; Design Automation segment already at 45% adjusted operating margin
Ansys cross-sell converts to revenue ahead of the $400M cumulative annual synergy target set for year four post-close, lifting non-GAAP operating margin above the guided ~41.5%
Design IP recovery sustains after returning to year-over-year growth in Q3 FY2026, removing the single biggest bear talking point
Agentic AI workflows built with Nvidia, Microsoft and AMD (early evaluations cut design cycle times ~25–40%) reprice Synopsys as an AI beneficiary rather than an AI victim
Deleveraging continues — $3.46B of debt repaid in 9M FY2026 — freeing FCF for buybacks against a ~3% FCF yield

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands near the guided $9.715B revenue and $15.07 non-GAAP EPS midpoints, FY2027 non-GAAP EPS reaches roughly the ~$17.7 implied Street average, and the multiple holds at 27–29x forward non-GAAP earnings. Ansys synergies arrive broadly on schedule, Design IP grows low-to-mid single digits, and China and export-control conditions neither improve nor deteriorate materially.

risks: AI coding and design agents compress seat counts and per-seat pricing, turning the EDA growth story into a share-of-workflow fight at 18–21x earnings
Ansys integration stalls — synergy slippage, sales-force disruption or churn in the simulation base — against $26.8B of goodwill and $11.5B of acquired intangibles
Renewed US export controls or a China demand air pocket reverses the Design IP recovery; management explicitly guides assuming no further export-control changes
Intel's foundry and design roadmap slips further, pressuring a large advanced-node customer
GAAP earnings stay near $4 per share while non-GAAP sits near $15, and investors start discounting the ~$1.6B annual intangible amortization and ~$950M stock compensation as real cost

catalysts.event: Q4 and full-year FY2026 results plus first FY2027 guidance — the key test of whether EDA double-digit growth and Ansys synergies carry into a clean post-integration year
Q1 FY2027 results — first quarter lapping a fully consolidated Ansys, so reported growth normalizes to organic
Completion of the Design IP portfolio reallocation and restructuring program ($380M–$410M of FY2026 charges) — margin proof point
Continued debt paydown and buyback execution under the $2.0B repurchase authorization replenished in February 2026
Target of $400M cumulative annual Ansys cost and revenue synergies
US export-control and Entity List changes affecting China EDA and IP sales — guidance assumes no further restrictions

key_risks: AI-driven disruption of the seat-based EDA licensing model — the dominant reason the stock de-rated in 2026
Ansys integration and synergy execution risk against $26.8B goodwill and $11.5B acquired intangibles
China export controls and Entity List restrictions; FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes no further tightening
Customer concentration among a small number of large semiconductor and hyperscaler customers, including Intel
$10.04B of total debt with ~$1.0B current, and ~$429M of interest expense in 9M FY2026
Wide GAAP-to-non-GAAP gap: ~$1.6B of annual intangible amortization and ~$950M of stock-based compensation
Design IP remains the volatile segment — it declined year over year for much of FY2026 before recovering in Q3
